title: PCI SSC calls for human approval of AI agent actions involving cardholder data
source_used: Help Net Security (fulltext, read in full)
key_facts: The PCI Security Standards Council published 'Security Considerations for AI Systems', guidance on protecting data given to AI systems in payment environments and defending against AI-assisted attacks.
The recommendations are advisory and existing PCI requirements take precedence.
For agents with access to readable (cleartext) cardholder data, explicit human approval for any action involving that data is recommended.
A 'least agency' approach limits each AI system to the access and abilities its task needs; a named human should accept responsibility for AI output.
AI systems should not handle, generate or manage unprotected passwords or cryptographic keys.
The Council warns AI can accelerate vulnerability discovery, exploit development and social engineering, and advises security and functional testing of AI-generated code and patches.
Organisations should avoid combining sensitive data access, external communications and untrusted input in one AI system.
quote_evidence: Its recommendations are advisory, and existing PCI requirements take precedence.

why_it_matters_hint: The body behind card-payment security rules sets out how AI agents should be restrained where card data is handled, though the advice is not mandatory.
